skim: Typhoon Dujuan killed at least two people and forced 1.6 million evacuations in Japan, while Germany’s AfD scored a third state election win as Chancellor Merz’s CDU collapsed to a post-war-low 4.9% in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Trump meets Zelensky in New York today ahead of Thursday’s Trump-Xi summit at the White House, where a ‘30 by 30’ tariff-reduction deal and a Taiwan arms-sale policy shift are both on the table.

Paramount sweetened its $111 billion bid for Warner Bros. Discovery with CNN editorial-independence guarantees after a 12-state lawsuit threatened the deal, and AMD crossed a $1 trillion market cap for the first time on renewed AI-chip demand.
Bangladesh’s measles death toll climbed past 1,063 as the outbreak that began in March rages on, and the UK filed its first-ever charges over the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
India’s Shafali Verma-led cricket team face Sri Lanka for Asian Games gold today, and Qatar’s Amir addresses the UN General Assembly amid a packed week of Gulf diplomacy in New York.

stories.headline: Typhoon Dujuan Batters Tokyo, Kills Two, Forces 1.6 Million to Evacuate
stories.body: Typhoon Dujuan slammed into Japan’s Kanto region with winds up to 144 km/h (89 mph), killing at least two people and triggering evacuation advisories for more than 1.6 million residents across Tokyo, Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures, per Al Jazeera (Sep 22). Flooding swamped the coastal city of Kamakura, where Mayor Takashi Matsuo warned “there is flooding in various parts of the city, so travelling by car is dangerous,” while Japan Airlines and ANA scrapped a combined 275 flights and bullet trains between Tokyo and Osaka were suspended. The Japan Meteorological Agency’s Takuya Hosomi cautioned there is “a risk the rain will continue” as the storm tracks north toward the Aleutian Islands.

stories.headline: Far-Right AfD Notches Third State Win as Germany’s CDU Suffers Historic Collapse
stories.body: Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won roughly 38% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania’s state election — its third state victory this year — while Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democrats (CDU) crashed from 13% to just 4.9%, the party’s worst result since World War II, losing every seat in the state parliament, per Axios (Sep 21). In Berlin’s simultaneous election, the Left party more than doubled its support to 25.7%, finishing first for the first time ever. AfD leader Alice Weidel declared her party had displaced the CDU as Germany’s “people’s party” and said the CDU “will have to think very carefully” about its firewall against cooperating with the far right, as Merz conceded “reforms have to come.”

stories.headline: Bangladesh’s Measles Death Toll Passes 1,060 as Outbreak Rages On
stories.body: Bangladesh’s measles death toll climbed to 1,063 after six more children died in the 24 hours ending Sep 21, with health authorities logging 1,221 new suspected cases and a cumulative 181,035 suspected cases nationwide since mid-March, per The Business Standard (Sep 21). Confirmed lab-verified infections have reached 20,646, with nearly 160,000 suspected patients hospitalized and infants under six months — too young to be vaccinated — among the hardest hit. Epidemiologist Prof Mahmudur Rahman said “from the beginning of the outbreak, we have not adequately implemented public health measures,” as the government’s catch-up vaccination drive struggles to keep pace.

stories.headline: Morocco Heads to the Polls in High-Stakes Parliamentary Vote
stories.body: Morocco holds parliamentary elections on Sep 23, with 27 political parties competing for 395 seats in the House of Representatives and roughly 15.8 million registered voters set to cast ballots, per Al Jazeera (Sep 21). Youth unemployment of 37.3% among 15-to-24-year-olds and rising living costs have dominated campaigning, with parties fanning out through markets and social media to court voters. Left Alliance candidate Fatima al-Tamni said “we do not want to speak to the citizen from above, nor turn the campaign into a festival of pictures and slogans,” while PJD campaign manager al-Wali al-Shtouki described mapping “spaces where citizens meet naturally.”

stories.headline: India Retain Rohit and Kohli for ODIs, Axe Pant for Irani Cup Captaincy
stories.body: India’s ODI squad for the West Indies series retained both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli as selectors eye the 2027 World Cup, while Rishabh Pant was dropped and instead named captain of Rest of India for the Irani Cup, per Business Standard (Sep 16). Hardik Pandya was also left out, with selectors wanting proof he can bowl a full 10 overs before a recall, as Dhruv Jurel was preferred as back-up wicketkeeper and uncapped duo Naman Dhir and Auqib Nabi earned maiden call-ups. Shubman Gill continues as captain with KL Rahul as his deputy for the three-match series starting Sep 27 in Thiruvananthapuram.

stories.headline: Ten-Man Real Madrid Fall to Atlético in Feisty Madrid Derby
stories.body: Atlético Madrid beat 10-man rivals Real Madrid 2-1 in a bad-tempered La Liga derby, with Alejandro Grimaldo converting a penalty and Jonathan David doubling the lead before Antonio Rüdiger’s late consolation, per Al Jazeera (Sep 20). Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half for hauling down Giuliano Simeone in the box, and Real’s front three of Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham were largely nullified. The win lifted Atlético to second in La Liga, five points behind leaders Barcelona and one above Real Madrid.

stories.headline: Cunha’s Late Strike Rescues Man Utd’s Worst Start in Years
stories.body: Manchester United fell behind to a Lisandro Martínez own goal before Matheus Cunha’s deflected strike in the 89th minute salvaged a 1-1 draw at Fulham, leaving United on just five points from five games — their joint-worst Premier League start — per Sky Sports (Sep 20). Martínez turned Calvin Bassey’s parried effort into his own net in the 63rd minute, and Cunha’s shot took a final deflection off David Affengruber to level it. The result leaves United stuck in the bottom half of the table heading into gameweek 6.

stories.headline: Verstappen Praises Norris’s New Junior Racing Team
stories.body: Max Verstappen backed Lando Norris’s newly launched junior outfit, LN4 Fusion, which will enter Formula 3 and other categories from 2027 to help fund young drivers without wealthy backers, per GPFans (Sep 21). “It’s tough at the moment, costs are rising. So the more you can help them, the better it is,” Verstappen said, adding of his own racing plans, “I enjoy the endurance side of things and combining endurance and Formula cars is very hectic.” The comments came in Baku race week, with speculation about Verstappen’s own Le Mans ambitions also swirling separately this week.

stories.headline: Paramount Sweetens Terms to Save $111 Billion Warner Bros. Discovery Takeover
stories.body: Paramount Skydance has agreed to concessions to salvage its $111 billion bid for Warner Bros. Discovery after a coalition of 12 Democratic state attorneys general sued to block the deal, per NPR (Sep 21). Per a person familiar with the arrangement, Paramount will run Warner Bros. and Paramount Pictures as separate studios releasing at least 30 films annually combined or face financial penalties, and will create a board to shield CNN’s newsroom from corporate editorial interference.

stories.headline: RBA’s Bullock Set to Address Markets as Rate Hike Odds Build for Next Week
stories.body: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock joins a CEDA-hosted fireside chat in Sydney today, one week before the RBA’s September 28-29 meeting where markets price roughly 70-75% odds of a 25-basis-point hike from the current 4.35%, per InvestingLive (Sep 21). Bullock recently told Parliament that “the upside inflation risks flagged in August are now materialising,” framing the key question as whether current tightening is enough to return inflation to target — remarks that have already firmed the Australian dollar.

stories.headline: Silver Nears Records, Gold Holds Above $4,300 as Summit Optimism Meets Fed Hikes
stories.body: Silver traded at $67.07/oz Monday morning, up roughly 5% on the week and 59.1% year-over-year, as investors weighed the U.N. General Assembly gathering and this week’s U.S.-China summit, per Yahoo Finance (Sep 21). Gold held above $4,300/oz even after the Fed’s rate hike, with Standard Chartered analysts noting “structural forces provide a solid floor” and fund manager Axel Merk arguing “disciplined monetary policy can’t fix fiscal risk,” per Kitco (Sep 21).

stories.headline: AMD Crosses $1 Trillion Market Cap for First Time
stories.body: AMD shares surged as much as 10% to an intraday record $613.92 on Monday, pushing its market capitalization past $1 trillion for the first time, per CNBC and Quartz (Sep 21). The milestone caps a five-session winning streak fueled by renewed AI chip demand, making AMD the latest chipmaker after Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron to join the trillion-dollar club.

stories.headline: SoftBank Launches $11 Billion Bond Sale to Fund Its OpenAI Bet
stories.body: SoftBank priced a combined $10 billion dollar-note and €1 billion euro-note offering — potentially the largest Asia-Pacific non-financial corporate bond deal on record — to cover its $10 billion contribution to OpenAI’s third investment tranche closing October 1, per Yahoo Finance/Quartz (Sep 21). Fitch assigned the debt a BB+ rating, and proceeds will also retire a $10 billion bridge loan SoftBank had taken out; pricing is set for Sep 24 with settlement Sep 29.

stories.headline: Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI Shopping Agent From Its Site
stories.body: Amazon cut off Meta’s new Muse AI agent from browsing or buying on Amazon.com, saying it never authorized Muse to access customer accounts, scrape listings or process transactions, per Axios (Sep 21). Amazon said such tools “should operate openly” and respect merchants’ choices; Meta did not respond to requests for comment, and the standoff comes as Muse became the #1 free app download across Apple and Google stores even though only 16% of shoppers say they trust AI to make purchases for them.

stories.headline: OpenAI Forms Math Advisory Group After AI Resolves 100+ Open Problems
stories.body: OpenAI announced a new mathematics advisory group hosted at Princeton’s Institute for Advanced Study to bridge the company with the mathematical community, per TechCrunch (Sep 21). The company says its AI model has resolved more than 100 open mathematics problems, prompting the initiative after controversy surrounding an earlier claimed solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem, though the institute clarified the group “will have no decision making power at any AI company.”

stories.headline: Trump, Zelensky Meet in New York Amid Push for an Energy-Strike Pause
stories.body: Trump and Zelensky are meeting Tuesday in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Zelensky saying the talks “could change a lot” and calling peace “Ukraine’s number one priority,” per Kyiv Independent (Sep 22). Zelensky plans to push for a mutual pause on strikes against energy infrastructure and Black Sea targets alongside continued air-defense support, while Trump has separately demanded Kyiv halt attacks on Russian oil refineries, citing the impact on global diesel prices.

stories.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Set for White House Thursday, ‘30 by 30’ Tariff Deal Expected
stories.body: Ahead of Thursday’s Trump-Xi summit at the White House — their third in-person meeting in under a year — both sides are finalizing a “30 by 30” deal to remove tariffs on $30 billion of goods each, per Atlantic Council (Sep 21). Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said “we are finding watermarks of our US large language models on many of the Chinese models, and that’s unacceptable,” underscoring AI competition as a flashpoint alongside Taiwan arms sales and stalled rare-earth commitments from the Busan truce. Trump has also signaled willingness to consult Beijing on future Taiwan arms sales, a shift from four decades of US policy.

stories.headline: Trump Weighs ‘Wiping Iran Out’ as UNGA Becomes Last Chance to Avert Escalation
stories.body: With the US-Israel war on Iran entering its seventh month, Trump told reporters he is weighing “wiping Iran out, letting them rot economically, or making a deal,” warning “very big things” could happen, while an IRGC spokesperson vowed renewed strikes would bring “new weapons and capabilities” that would “change the weapons and geography of the war,” per Time (Sep 21). Gulf mediators are shuttling proposals between Washington and Tehran to revive talks, though Iran has conditioned negotiations on an end to the war and the lifting of naval blockades. International Crisis Group’s Ali Vaez called this week’s UN gathering “the last best opportunity to prevent escalation,” but warned “very serious differences, and deep mistrust” make a breakthrough unlikely.

stories.headline: Turkey, Pakistan Activate Mutual Defense Pact as Houthi Attacks Batter Saudi Arabia
stories.body: As Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensify — the group claimed 26 attacks in 24 hours, per Al Jazeera reporting — Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Ankara stands ready to meet Riyadh’s military needs under the trilateral Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed August 7 with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, per Al Jazeera (Sep 19). “They may have some military needs, especially on some technical issues. We would have no issues in meeting these,” Fidan said. Pakistan’s Lt.-Gen. Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry separately pledged to defend Saudi Arabia “to any extent,” under a pact that treats an attack on any of the three members as an attack on all.

stories.headline: Gaza Peace Board to Brief World Leaders as Israel Stalls on Hamas Disarmament Plan
stories.body: Trump’s Board of Peace will brief dozens of countries, EU officials and a committee of Palestinian technocrats on Gaza reconstruction September 23 on the sidelines of UNGA, but 71 proposed rebuilding projects still lack a start date because Israel has rejected the Board’s Hamas disarmament roadmap, per Times of Israel (Sep 18). Hamas agreed to disarmament terms on July 30, and Board officials reportedly believe Israeli cooperation is more likely only after Israel’s October 27 Knesset election. The session will cover the disarmament roadmap, near-term priorities, and future reconstruction phases.

fixtures.headline: Asian Games Gold Medal Final: India v Sri Lanka
fixtures.body: India, fresh off Shafali Verma’s record century, face Sri Lanka for the women’s cricket gold medal today at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan. Sri Lanka reached the final by beating Pakistan by eight wickets in the other semi-final.

fixtures.headline: India Open ODI Series vs West Indies
fixtures.body: India begin a three-match ODI series against West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram, with Shubman Gill captaining a squad that retains Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli and controversially omits Rishabh Pant and Hardik Pandya.

fixtures.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix Moves to a Saturday
fixtures.body: F1 heads to Baku for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the race itself shifted to Saturday for the first time to avoid a clash with the country’s Remembrance Day on September 27 — only the second Saturday race on the calendar after Las Vegas.

portfolio.headline: Arm Holdings Rallies on Fresh Analyst Coverage and New AI Chip Designs
portfolio.body: Piper Sandler initiated coverage on Arm with an Overweight rating and a $320 price target, citing “strong momentum in server CPU design wins,” while Raymond James lifted its target to $272 from $244 on expanding server royalty exposure. The moves coincided with Arm unveiling new AI-optimized silicon, the Neoverse CSS N4 and an “Arm AGI CPU,” with CEO Rene Haas telling CNBC that “demand for Arm technology is at record levels.” Per StocksToTrade (Sep 21).

portfolio.headline: Intel Jumps on SK Hynix Talks, AI Turnaround Optimism, and CPU Price Hikes
portfolio.body: Intel shares climbed on reports the company is in talks with SK Hynix over U.S. memory-chip production at a future Ohio facility, alongside a string of analyst target hikes — Tigress Financial raised its target to $145, citing “an AI-driven turnaround, stronger Xeon demand, solid 18A execution,” while Northland upgraded the stock to Outperform with a $120 target on server CPU shortages. Separately, Intel’s High-NA EUV process crossed one million wafers processed, and reports pointed to a planned 10% PC CPU price increase in October. Per StocksToTrade (Sep 21).

portfolio.headline: Fastly Unveils an AI Firewall to Block Prompt-Injection Attacks
portfolio.body: Fastly introduced three new AI-focused products — an AI Firewall to block prompt-injection and other attacks on language models, an AI Runtime Control layer for managing token spending and failover, and an API Security tool for agent traffic. Chief Product Officer Kelly Shortridge said “enterprises adopting coding agents and artificial intelligence features need control in production, at runtime, without delay.” The launch carries no disclosed customer contracts yet. Per 24/7 Wall St (Sep 21).

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare Catches the Same AI-Security Wave as Fastly
portfolio.body: Cloudflare shares moved higher alongside rival Fastly’s Sep 21 launch of new AI-focused security tools, as the sector broadly re-rated on growing enterprise demand for products that police AI agent and large-language-model traffic. No distinct Cloudflare-specific announcement accompanied the move; it tracked the wider AI-infrastructure security theme that also lifted Datadog. Per 24/7 Wall St (Sep 21).

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Gets a Bigger Price Target From Bank of America
portfolio.body: Bank of America raised its price target on CrowdStrike to $260 from $230 on Sep 20 while maintaining a Neutral rating, part of a broader Wall Street debate over the cybersecurity firm’s valuation after shares approached 52-week highs. Per Ad-Hoc News (Sep 20).

portfolio.headline: Sonos Rides Its Hardware and Software Relaunch
portfolio.body: Sonos has been benefiting from investor enthusiasm for its new “Sonos 27” software platform and a refreshed hardware lineup including the Beam Ultra and Ace Ultra speakers, part of a broader brand relaunch the company kicked off earlier this month. No fresh company-specific announcement was tied to today’s session; the move looks like a continuation of that early-September product-cycle story rather than a new catalyst. Per Simply Wall St (Sep 15).

portfolio.headline: Twilio Keeps Re-Rating Without an Obvious New Catalyst
portfolio.body: No company-specific news or analyst action was found tied to Twilio’s session. GuruFocus (Sep 21) flagged the move as occurring even as its valuation model shows the stock trading well above fair value, with insiders having been net sellers over the past year. The gain looks like a continuation of investor enthusiasm since Twilio’s summer guidance raise rather than a new development.

stories.headline: Jaishankar Pushes ‘Reformed Multilateralism’ at UN Amid Fuel-Food-Finance Crunch
stories.body: Speaking at the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism Summit during UNGA81, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar warned that “we meet at a time when the global order is under stress” and that the “four ‘F crisis’ of Fuel, food, fertiliser and finance cannot be left to itself,” per WION (Sep 22). He said “Reformed Multilateralism is therefore essential,” and separately held bilateral talks with Switzerland and Nauru while joining the first Visegrád Group–India Foreign Ministers’ meeting, where the V4 bloc backed India’s bid for a permanent UN Security Council seat.

stories.headline: Two Infants Die as Fire Guts Newborn Care Unit at Telangana Hospital
stories.body: A blaze tore through the Special Newborn Care Unit at Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences in Adilabad, Telangana late Monday night, killing two infants though 28 other children were evacuated safely, per WION (Sep 22). Preliminary findings point to an electrical short circuit in an air conditioner; Chief Minister Revanth Reddy ordered a detailed inquiry and directed officials to “ensure that all children affected by the incident receive the best possible medical care” while tightening hospital fire-safety rules statewide.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi Demands POCSO Action After Bihar Teens Assaulted on Video
stories.body: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi demanded that “every individual in that video must be identified and prosecuted under POCSO” after footage surfaced of a 15-year-old girl being groped and a boy dragged off his bike by six to seven men in Jamui, Bihar on Sep 19, per WION (Sep 21). Three minors have been arrested, but Gandhi pressed the state government, asking “why a girl is not safe on a public road at 7 pm,” calling the incident a matter of patriarchal control rather than culture.

stories.headline: UK Charges First Suspect Over 1994 Rwandan Genocide
stories.body: British prosecutors charged Vincent Brown, 65 — formerly known as Vincent Bajinya — with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six counts of aiding crimes against humanity, marking the first-ever UK charges tied to the Rwandan genocide, per Al Jazeera (Sep 21). Crown Prosecution Service counterterror chief Frank Ferguson said “this is the first time charges relating to the genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda have been brought in the United Kingdom,” after Metropolitan Police war crimes investigators reopened the case in 2019 following a blocked 2017 extradition to Rwanda.

stories.headline: Burnham Approves RAF Refuelling Support for Saudi Jets Fighting Houthi Attacks
stories.body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he agreed overnight to a Saudi request for an RAF Voyager aircraft to refuel Saudi jets flying defensive missions against Houthi missile and drone strikes, stating “on the advice of the defence secretary and the foreign secretary, last night I agreed to that request for defensive air-to-air refuelling,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 22). He framed the time-limited deal as protecting Red Sea shipping lanes carrying roughly 12% of global trade, days after Houthi forces intercepted a missile aimed at Riyadh on Sep 19 and seized the port of Mocha.

stories.headline: Qatar’s Amir Set to Address UN General Assembly on Regional Crises
stories.body: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani heads Qatar’s delegation to the 81st UN General Assembly and is scheduled to address the opening session on Tuesday, Sep 22, focusing on “prominent issues, especially those related to regional and international affairs,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 21). The address follows a run of high-level Qatari diplomacy in New York, with ministers holding parallel bilateral meetings on the sidelines of UNGA81.

stories.headline: Qatar’s PM Holds Five Bilateral Meetings With Foreign Ministers at UNGA
stories.body: Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani met separately in New York with the foreign ministers of Mexico, Canada, Cyprus, Estonia and Austria to discuss “bilateral cooperation and the means to enhance them, in addition to several regional and international issues of joint interest,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 22). The run of meetings came as Qatar’s delegation kept a packed schedule on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.

stories.headline: Qatar’s PM Calls for Gulf-Iran Security Framework After War’s Fallout
stories.body: Speaking at the Qatar Economic Forum in New York, Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani said “the Gulf won’t be the same unless there’s a framework ensuring no one is a threat to each other,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 20). He argued the post-conflict Gulf needs new mechanisms allowing Gulf states and Iran to coexist and cooperate, distinct from his earlier “earthquake” remarks on the Iran war’s fallout.

doha_events.headline: Eat Spain Drink Spain Qatar 2026
doha_events.body: A month-long celebration of Spanish food and culture runs at venues across Qatar from Sep 20–Oct 4, free to attend, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: Sid Sriram Live in Doha
doha_events.body: Indian playback singer Sid Sriram performs at Exhibition Hall 7, Qatar National Convention Centre, on Sep 25, with tickets from QAR 220 via Platinumlist, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: The Mentalist Suhani Shah Live in Qatar
doha_events.body: Mentalist Suhani Shah brings her live mind-reading show to the Conference Hall at QNCC on Sep 25, with tickets from QAR 100 via Platinumlist, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: John Achkar Stand-Up: Feena Nehke?
doha_events.body: Lebanese comedian John Achkar performs his stand-up show “Feena Nehke?” at Abdul Aziz Nasser Theatre on Sep 25 (two showtimes), with tickets from QAR 195 via Platinumlist, per Qatar Living.

doha_events.headline: AFRO Waves Pool Party at Desert Falls
doha_events.body: AFRO Waves brings an Afrobeat-themed pool day to the Sea Caves area of Desert Falls Water & Adventure Park on Sep 25, with entry at QAR 99 via Q-Tickets, per Qatar Living.
